sentences.text: Lusonectes is an extinct genus of pliosauroid that lived during the Early Jurassic in Portugal.
The genus is defined by a unique broad triangular parasphenoid cultriform process and a specific combination of skull features.
Lusonectes possessed slender, conical teeth with circular cross-sections.
Lusonectes is the only known diagnostic plesiosaur from Portugal to date.
It stands as the first diagnostic plesiosaur species identified in Portugal.
The generic name Lusonectes combines the Latin prefix for Portugal and the Greek word for swimmer.
The species name sauvagei honors Henri Émile Sauvage, who first described the holotype.
The holotype specimen MG33 was discovered in the 19th century near Alhadas, Portugal, by geologist Paul Choffat and his team.
Adam S. Smith, Ricardo Araújo, and Octávio Mateus formally named the genus Lusonectes in 2012.
While originally classified as a plesiosaurid, Lusonectes has uncertain affinities with microcleidids or early pliosaurids due to fragmentary fossils.
A 2026 study found that Lusonectes' placement varies depending on the phylogenetic analysis method used.
Some analyses place Lusonectes among early plesiosauroids, while others suggest it is an early-diverging pliosaurid near Thalassiodracon hawkinsii.
Lusonectes lived during the Toarcian stage of the Early Jurassic in the São Gião Formation of Portugal.
Lusonectes lived between 184.2 and 174.7 million years ago.
Only one fossil occurrence of Lusonectes has been recorded.
The environment where Lusonectes lived experienced periodic oxygen depletion during the Toarcian Oceanic Anoxic Event.
Researchers note that the unstable relationships of early plesiosaurs and poor fossil preservation limit confidence in Lusonectes' precise classification.
